headline: Nijman averages 110.56 and still loses to Coates
standfirst: The world number ten played his best darts of the week and went home anyway, beaten 6-3 by debutant Henry Coates, ranked 76 places below him.
body: Wessel Nijman averaged 110.56 at Butlins on Friday night. That is the best average of the Players Championship Finals so far, and it was not enough. Henry Coates, the world number 86 on his debut, beat him 6-3.

Nijman did the flashy stuff. He won legs in 11 darts twice, and the crowd knew they were watching something special. Coates just kept answering. He averaged 93.73, roughly in line with his 12-month figure of 94.33, and still found the doubles when they mattered: 85.7 per cent of them, which means he barely missed all night.

The turning point came early. Coates broke in the second leg with a 58 out in 12 darts, and Nijman spent the rest of the night chasing. Later came a 96 finish, then a 95, then a 105 to make it 5-2. Nijman took one more leg and the match was gone.
Nijman's doubles were the problem: 50 per cent, and his highest checkout of the night was only 46. Brilliant scoring, nothing to finish it with. It is the oldest darts story there is.
Coates banks at least £7,000 and meets Gabriel Clemens in the last 32 on Saturday. Nijman leaves with £4,000 and a very good average to think about on the drive home.
Our view: Coates will not be frightened by anybody now. You do not get much more daunting than an average like that coming at you from the other end of the oche.
